As of 2/11/2026, CritEngine uses refl-cpp for its reflection needs. These are notes related to the  library to help better understand its usage and how it works.

# Logical Heirarchy

This section is focused on building intuition for the refl-cpp library by introducing the classes
following a dependency chain.

## refl_impl::metadata::type_info__\<T>
* The most fundamental type that represents other types.
* Is internal to the library and isn't used directly by users.
* Specializations are generated by provided reflection macros.
* Base template is marked invalid through the presence of the "invalid_marker" field.
    * Specializations do not contain the invalid marker, which is how **is_reflectable\<T>** 
      finds what can or cannot be reflected.

## refl::detail::type_info\<T>
* Acts as an alias for refl_impl::metadata::type_info__\<T>.

## refl::descriptor::type_descriptor\<T>
* Wraps refl::detail::type_info\<T> as a private field.
* Statically Asserts that type T **is_reflectable\<T>**
* Notably, contains typedefs related to class inheritance

## refl::descriptor::base_member_descriptor\<T>
* Wraps refl::detail::type_descriptor\<T> as a private field.

# Usage

As reflection is used for both introspection and intercession, both goals differ in usage.
Introspection requires less setup as all that is needed is to read type information 
and make decisions based on them.
Intercession requires the presence of objects and type_descriptors to modify reflected data.

refl::detail::type_info\<T> can provide the ability to do introspection 
and support invalid cases such as a representing a non-reflected type.

refl::descriptor::type_descriptor\<T> and its derivatives allows both 
introspection and intercession at the tradeoff that invalid cases are unrepresentable and lead to compile errors.
